build.paradigm: round3 rust_pcor_v2 (python-source __init__ via importlib; maturin -i sys.executable; PATH=/root/.cargo/bin)

upstream.package: GENIE3 1.24.0 (Bioconductor 3.18; installed R lib version matches)
upstream.note: CRAN 404s (GENIE3 lives on Bioconductor); the version suggested in the task brief (1.24.0) is archived there. Local installed R GENIE3 == 1.24.0, so the port targets the exact binary the campaign's R reference will run.
upstream.r_version_rng_reference: R 4.3.3 installed locally (runif ground truth), RNG.c from R-4-3-branch (wch/r-source mirror)

c_to_rust_map.rust: genie3.rs Core::build (param init, identity ls/weights, maxnodes=nbterms*(2*nbobj-1), ensemble, re-sort attribute_vector, importance)
c_to_rust_map.notes: object_mapping is identity in GENIE3 and never mutated -> dropped; node_weight/node_size/prediction tables write-only in this configuration -> dropped (documented no-ops)

stack order preserved: left pushed first, right on top (right processed next); empty children become leaves via nodesize<min_node_size short-circuit exactly like C; stop-condition short-circuit order (nodesize==1 || nodesize<1 || stop_splitting) preserved so v_tot is only set when C sets it
two-pointer partition on check_test(val<thr); returns start+1 iff ls[start] passes; used for both build (on cls) and importance (on ts_vector)

verbatim: insertion sort with VAL<=a break, median-of-3 with the three swaps, do-while scan loops, ir-i+1>=j-l stack order, and the C early-return when jstack>50 (leaves segment partially sorted - bug-compatible). istack sized 52 vs C's 50: C writes istack[50] OOB in the unreachable jstack==50 corner; Rust cannot UB there, reachable behaviour identical
GENIE3 uses numerical attributes only (attribute_descriptors all 0)

RF path: one get_random_integer per loop iteration; swap selected attribute to position remaining_att-1; attribute_vector permutation PERSISTS across nodes and trees (C never resets inside BuildTreeEns); ET path: do-while with nb_try decrement on score<0 and threshold 10.0
R-package variant: rn = unif_rand()*RAND_MAX(2147483647); floor(rn*max_val*1.0/(RAND_MAX+1.0)); float variant casts to f32
core_table att-major f32 == c(x) column-major layout of exprMatrixT[, regs]
bagging consumes exactly n draws; weights zeroed then +1.0 per draw; ls keeps objects with weight!=0 in id order

CRITICAL stream detail: make_ls_vector(-1) BEFORE tree 0 and once per tree AFTER building (loop body order: build -> make_ls_vector -> store), so n_trees+1 bootstrap vectors are drawn; the final one is discarded but advances the stream for the NEXT target gene's .C call
accumulation `w*y*y` == (w*y)*y in f64 (left-assoc, y promoted once)
op order: t2[0] then per-goal t2[2i+1], t2[2i+2], y/n var with fabs, info=v_tot-(y+n), return info/v_tot (v_tot global set by stop_splitting at this node)
sets v_tot WITHOUT fabs; leaf iff (v_tot/t0[0])<=0.0
NaN-safe in the same direction as C (NaN>=0 false -> leaf)

MIXED PRECISION SITE: `tsm[1][2] += w*(y*y)` with y*y rounded in f32 FIRST; threshold midpoint `(float)((old+new as f32)/2.0)` then `if old>=bt: bt=new`; strict > for score improvement; best_score>=0.0 gate at the end
one get_random_float when min!=max; threshold = max-(max-min)*rf in f32; accumulation here is `w*y*y` == (w*y)*y f64 (site A, differs from the RF threshold scan!)
per-goal v_tot computed inside the loop; vi = v_tot-(fabs+fabs)
MIXED PRECISION SITE: `tsm[..][2] += y*y` with the product rounded in f32, then promoted; weights are ++ (+=1.0); empty-side guard (start>=borne || borne>end) -> vi=0
obj=-1 path; children pushed only when non-empty (start<borne, borne<=end); left then right (right processed next); nodesize==1 or leaf -> pop
ts_vector=identity; attribute_position identity (attribute_vector was re-sorted by BuildTreeEns before this call); sum_weight=n_trees; final /=sum_weight

c_to_rust_map.rust: EnsParams { n_trees, rf_k, et, bootstrap, min_node_size=1 }
c_to_rust_map.notes: compile-time configuration instead of function pointers; savepred=0, varmin=0.0

per-target setdiff(regulatorNames, targetName) preserving order (R setdiff dedups, first occurrence kept); mtry=.setMtry per target; weight matrix rows=regulatorNames input order; im/sum(im) column normalization
K numeric -> K; 'sqrt' -> round(sqrt(p)) (R round, NOT floor - this fixes a semantic error carried in round3 py_genie3 which used floor); else p

rng.target: R 4.3 default RNGkind: Mersenne-Twister via unif_rand(), as consumed by GENIE3.c after set.seed()
set_seed_path: n_seed=625: 625 further LCG steps fill i_seed[0..624]

NOTE: MT_sgenrand() exists in RNG.c but is NOT on the set.seed path - the state is the raw LCG stream. A first implementation that used MT_sgenrand (scrambled or not) failed the R reference values; the i_seed path matches bit-exactly.
rng.unif_rand: fixup(MT_genrand()); MT_genrand = tempered y * 2^-32 (literal 2.3283064365386963e-10); fixup replaces x<=0 with 0.5*i2_32m1 and (1-x)<=0 with 1-0.5*i2_32m1 (literal 2.328306437080797e-10)
consumption_order: per target (= per .C BuildTreeEns call): bootstrap0 (n draws) -> per tree t: one get_random_integer per find_the_best_split_among_k iteration (i.e. mtry per split node, fewer only when the attribute pool empties) -> bootstrap(t+1) (n draws) drawn AFTER building tree t
the bootstrap after the LAST tree is drawn and discarded (C loop calls make_ls_vector(current_tree) unconditionally) but advances the stream for the next target
ET: no bootstrap (identity ls); draws only in find_a_split_at_random_et (one randint + one randfloat per non-constant attribute evaluation)
rng.norm_rand: not needed - GENIE3.c uses unif_rand() only

validation.method: bit-exact equality with installed R 4.3.3 runif after set.seed

float_semantics.storage: X and Y stored f32 exactly as R's as.single at the .C boundary (f64->f32 round-to-nearest, applied per value in the Python wrapper via a single ascontiguousarray(..., dtype=float32))
float_semantics.accumulators: SCORE_TYPE=double; all table_score_multiregr arithmetic in f64
mixed_sites: find_the_best_threshold_multiregr: w*(y*y) - y*y FIRST rounded in f32 then f64 multiply
get_vi_multiregr_separate: y*y in f32 promoted by the += (counts incremented as +=1.0)
threshold midpoint: float add -> double /2.0 -> round to f32 -> old_val>=bt check in f32
ET random threshold: max-(max-min)*get_random_float() entirely in f32
float_semantics.x87_assumption: C compiled with default x86-64 SSE2 semantics (FLT_EVAL_METHOD=0): float+float computes in float. All f32 arithmetic above assumes this; the R package .so is built the same way
float_semantics.wrapper_normalization: im <- im/sum(im): R sum() accumulates doubles in long double (x87 80-bit) sequentially; emulated exactly in rng.rs X87 (exponent diff <=64 handled exactly in u128, diff >=65 provably rounds away with no tie possible; final round to f64 = one further RNE at 53 bits, like an x87 store). Reached regime (importance magnitudes) exact; f64-subnormal far-tail (e < -1021 intermediate rounding during the final powi-based scale) not perfectly emulated - unreachable for variance-reduction sums

parity.threads: always 1 (n_threads accepted and ignored - verified by smoke [3a])
parity.stream: ONE RMersenneTwister seeded via the set.seed path, shared sequentially across targets in targetNames order - replicates R's global RNG state across successive .C calls
parity.claim: bit-level replica of R GENIE3 1.24.0 single-core execution from set.seed(seed) onward, subject to the assumptions in float_semantics

fast.parallelism: rayon across targets; each target's forest is independent
fast.stream: per-target RMersenneTwister seeded with the high 32 bits of SplitMix64(master_seed mixed with ordinal+1) fed through the SAME set.seed initialization path
fast.deviation_nature: identical algorithm and identical per-target computation given the draws; ONLY the bootstrap/attribute-subset draw sequences differ from parity (independent streams instead of one shared sequential stream). Deterministic and thread-count-invariant. Verified: corr(fast(seed=1), parity(seed=1)) == corr(parity(seed=2), parity(seed=1)) within noise (0.747 vs 0.741 at 100 trees) - fast behaves exactly like the same algorithm on an independent stream

entry_semantics.orientation: exp = genes x samples (rows genes); internally transposed to samples x genes f32
entry_semantics.regulators: None -> all genes; names (validated, order preserved) or 1-based integer positions (R semantics)
entry_semantics.per_target: setdiff(regulatorNames, targetName) - order preserved, dedup, self removed (self-loop weight 0)
entry_semantics.n_trees: default 1000 (R default); nmin=1; bootstrap (RF); IncNodePurity importance; double normalization (C: /sum_tree_weights, wrapper: /sum(im) with long-double sum)
entry_semantics.exp_cutoff: infer_weight_exp_mat_genie3 replicates inferWeightExpMat: =0 keeps rowSums>0 rows; (0,1) and >=1 branches as in round3 py_genie3
entry_semantics.degenerate: constant-y target -> importance all 0 -> 0/0 = NaN column (same as R); 0 regulators for a target (RF) -> zero column, 2n stream draws consumed (matches R running the C on empty input); 0 regulators in ET refused (C would be UB)

layers: [1] MT RNG bit-exact vs R 4.3.3 runif (seeds 1/123/42)
[2] Rust parity == independent Python transliteration of GENIE3.c, bit-exact, 20 targets x 19 regs x 5 trees (both implementations written from the C source; catches porting slips)
[3a] parity twice-run bit-identical; n_threads=8 does not change parity; non-degenerate columns sum to 1; self-loops 0
[3b] fast deterministic + thread-invariant; stream-noise equivalence vs parity documented above
[3c] fast single-target == Python transliteration seeded with the same SplitMix64-derived seed, bit-exact
[4] wrapper semantics: mtry round vs floor distinguishes p=3; setdiff order; exp_cutoff rowSums>0; constant-y NaN column; ET path runs; infer_weight_exp_mat end-to-end
smoke.no_R_GENIE3_reference_used: per task constraints (runs/ untouched; no GENIE3 result compared against R output). RNG-level validation against installed R behavior is the explicitly permitted exception ('或用已安装 R 的行为验证')

uncertainties: Bit-level parity vs the R binary rests on (a) FLT_EVAL_METHOD=0 for the C build (SSE2 default), (b) glibc RAND_MAX=2147483647, (c) R sum() long-double accumulation as emulated. All three hold for the local R 4.3.3 / gcc toolchain; the campaign's reference must run on the same class of platform.
R GENIE3's foreach path (nCores>1) uses doRNG - NOT replicated (out of scope; campaign reference is single-core c1).
ET path ported and structurally validated but not bit-checked against a second transliteration in smoke; RF is the campaign path.
save_ensemble_ls tables (never read by the importance computation) are not materialized - zero effect on RNG or numerics.
node_weight/node_size/prediction arrays are write-only in this configuration - dropped with no behavioural effect.
